title: Measure the grader
purpose: Enable a learner to turn the human labels and judge predictions produced in EP-01 and EP-02 into a trustworthy grader report that exposes the confusion matrix and prints precision and recall for the defined regression class.
prerequisites: The learner can read and edit basic Python and run Jupyter notebook cells.
The learner understands that human_label = 1 and judge_label = 1 mean the defined regression is present.
build/lesson-01/eval_cases.jsonl and build/lesson-02/judge_predictions.jsonl exist with the approved stable case IDs and binary-label semantics.

user_stories.title: Join evidence by identity
user_stories.statement: As an eval maintainer, I want to join human labels and judge predictions by case ID so that row order cannot silently change which prediction is scored against which reference.
user_stories.one_idea: A grader must align reference labels and predictions by stable identity and reject missing, duplicate, unknown, or contradictory records before counting outcomes.
acceptance_criteria: The grader loads both prior artifacts and joins records by case_id rather than list position.
Validation rejects duplicate, missing, or unknown case IDs and any copied human_label that differs between artifacts.
The joined records preserve the invariant that label 1 means regression present.

user_stories.title: Count the four outcomes
user_stories.statement: As an evaluator, I want to classify every joined record as TP, FP, FN, or TN so that the aggregate score remains traceable to concrete cases.
user_stories.one_idea: The confusion matrix is a partition of aligned binary decisions whose four counts must sum to the number of scored cases.
acceptance_criteria: The lesson defines TP, FP, FN, and TN using regression present as the positive class.
Each joined case is assigned to exactly one outcome and remains inspectable by case_id.
The grader verifies that TP + FP + FN + TN equals the number of joined cases.

user_stories.title: Read precision and recall
user_stories.statement: As an AI feature owner, I want precision and recall tied to operational questions so that I can distinguish false alarms from missed regressions.
user_stories.one_idea: Precision measures how often regression alarms are correct, while recall measures how many human-labeled regressions the judge catches.
acceptance_criteria: Precision is computed as TP / (TP + FP) and recall as TP / (TP + FN).
The lesson connects false positives to false alarms and false negatives to missed regressions without collapsing the two metrics into accuracy.
Both formulas define zero-division behavior explicitly as 0.0 and the report records that policy.

user_stories.title: Prove and persist the grader report
user_stories.statement: As an eval maintainer, I want deterministic expected values and a persisted report so that the final metrics can be reproduced and audited offline.
user_stories.one_idea: A metric pipeline is trustworthy only when a known fixture proves its counts and derived values and the same checked result is persisted.

checkpoints.capability: Build a confusion matrix from judge predictions and print precision and recall with zero-division handling.
checkpoints.observable_check: After completing US-L03-01 through US-L03-04, a fresh-kernel notebook run joins at least 10 prior-artifact records by case_id, validates label alignment, prints the fixture's TP, FP, FN, TN, precision, and recall, writes grader_report.json, reloads it, and ends with PASS.

acceptance_criteria: The deterministic fixture contains at least 10 unique case IDs and produces exact predeclared TP, FP, FN, TN, precision, and recall values.
grader_report.json contains the positive-class definition, zero-division policy, case count, all four counts, precision, and recall.
The persisted report is reloaded and compared with the checked in-memory result before a final PASS is printed.

visible_checks: Load both prior artifacts, assert and print that each contains at least 10 records, and print the inherited positive-class definition.
Validate binary labels, unique IDs, exact case-ID coverage, and matching copied human labels; join by case_id and print PASS.
Classify each case as TP, FP, FN, or TN, print the case-level outcomes, and prove that the four counts sum to the joined case count.
Compute and print precision and recall with an explicit 0.0 zero-division policy; assert exact predeclared fixture counts and metric values over at least 10 case IDs.
Write grader_report.json, reload and compare it with the in-memory report, print the output path, and end with a final PASS.
build_along.offline_replay: The canonical Jupyter notebook uses Python 3.12 and only the repository-contained EP-01 and EP-02 artifacts. From a fresh kernel it validates and joins records by case_id, computes and verifies the confusion matrix, precision, and recall, persists and reloads grader_report.json, and prints all declared checks without network access, API keys, model weights, or paid calls. The executed notebook and actual output are recorded under output/lesson-03/.

capstone_trace: CONTEXT.md breaking point 3 identifies the learner failure addressed by this epic: aggregate accuracy can hide missed regressions or excessive false alarms. US-L03-02 exposes the four outcomes and US-L03-03 separates those costs through precision and recall.
CP-L03-03-A directly completes the capstone by producing a working grader that prints a confusion matrix, precision, and recall for the explicitly defined positive class with zero-division handling.
The grader consumes both approved upstream artifacts, joins by stable case_id, and verifies copied human labels so the cumulative build does not restart or silently alter EP-01 and EP-02 semantics.
build/lesson-03/grader_report.json is the final cumulative artifact and is independently useful as an auditable machine-readable summary of the grader's population, policy, counts, and metrics.

The fixture contains at least 10 stable case IDs and provides a deterministic capstone oracle with predeclared TP, FP, FN, TN, precision, and recall; count conservation plus report round-trip checks make the printed result reproducible and give the metrics a useful sample.

Searcher brief: research only EP-03 claims needed to define binary confusion-matrix outcomes, precision, recall, positive-class interpretation, and explicit zero-division behavior; write only agent/evals-course-factory/output/lesson-03/searcher/sources.json. Do not research or draft broader metric catalogs, threshold tuning, multiclass evaluation, lesson prose, notebook code, or live-provider integrations.

Builder brief: consume only this approved plan, approved EP-03 research, build/lesson-01/eval_cases.jsonl, and build/lesson-02/judge_predictions.jsonl; write course/lesson-03.md plus the notebook and persisted grader report under build/lesson-03/, with actual executed results only under output/lesson-03/. As explicitly requested by the human, expand the cumulative fixture chain to at least 10 stable case IDs by minimally updating the EP-01 dataset/notebook/executed output and the corresponding EP-02 cached responses/predictions/notebook/executed output while preserving schemas, label semantics, lesson flow, and existing user edits. Preserve four text-only, one-idea Lesson 03 sections of 300-500 words and about 2-3 minutes each, followed by exactly one incremental build-along of at most 20 minutes. Use an editable Jupyter notebook that runs offline top-to-bottom from a fresh kernel on Python 3.12, prints every declared visible check, joins by case_id, preserves label semantics, asserts at least 10 cases, and persists grader_report.json. Do not use Mermaid, raster images, quizzes, flashcards, video, audio, paid calls, model weights, live-provider integration, multiclass metrics, or threshold tuning.
